# Think Operator

> Business judgment practice for owners, operators, and CEOs. Read a decision framework, then practice it with a quiz or scenario.

The site is a static export. Assessment scores and practice history are calculated and stored in the browser. Scores are practice feedback, not a professional certification or a validated hiring assessment. Optional public leaderboard posting is separate.

## Start here

- [Guide hub](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/): 35 practical frameworks grouped into hiring, finance, ops cadence, strategy, and people.
- [Test hub](https://thinkoperator.com/tests/): what each existing quiz and scenario set tests.
- [Daily Decision](https://thinkoperator.com/daily/): one dated prompt and a browser-local streak.

## Decision guides

- [What to Do When Your Best Employee Quits](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/what-to-do-when-your-best-employee-quits/): When your best employee quits, do not counter in the doorway. Protect the work within 48 hours, transfer what they know, then decide whether the role returns.
- [How to Delegate as a Business Owner](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-delegate/): Delegate frequent work you already understand. Hand off the outcome, the limit, and a review date. Inspect the finished result instead of every keystroke.
- [When to Hire Your First Employee](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/when-to-hire-your-first-employee/): Hire when you turn away paid work or repeat tasks fill the week. Price the full cost against the hours or revenue freed. Hire the bottleneck, not comfort.
- [How to Price a Service Business](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-price-a-service-business/): Price a service from hours you can sell and the pay you must cover, then check the market and the job's worth. A near-perfect close rate means the price is low.
- [How to Improve Cash Flow in a Small Business](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-improve-cash-flow/): Profit is not cash. Collect what you are owed, take deposits on lumpy jobs, and time bills. Build a 13-week view before you cut what creates the next sale.
- [How to Find the Bottleneck in Your Business](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-find-the-bottleneck/): The bottleneck is where the queue keeps growing, not the busiest person. Measure what each step finishes. Improve that step, pace the others, and spend last.
- [Why Is My Business Not Growing](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/why-is-my-business-not-growing/): Growth stalls in one place: demand, conversion, capacity, delivery, retention, or you. Put one number on each and fix the branch that is actually stuck.
- [How to Prioritize as a Business Owner](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-prioritize/): Rank work by revenue, margin, cash, or risk, then by effort. Loud tasks can wait. When you add a commitment, name what drops. Review the short list weekly.
- [Why Are Sales Down](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/why-are-sales-down/): Sales equal traffic times conversion times order value times repeat buys. Find which term moved before changing the offer. A floor story is a clue, not a plan.
- [How to Get More Customers for a Small Business](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-get-more-customers/): Win customers through the channel they already use. Ask for referrals, contact lapsed buyers, then test one new channel. Keep it if they are worth the cost.
- [How to Create SOPs and Systemize Your Business](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-create-sops/): Write procedures for tasks that pull you back in. Record the work, turn it into a short page, and have someone else run it. Name an owner and a review date.
- [How to Scale Operations Without Losing Quality](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-scale-operations/): Keep quality as you grow by standardizing the work, checking each handoff, and watching rework. Automate a step only after it is stable. Volume multiplies mess.
- [Should I Raise Prices](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/should-i-raise-prices/): Raise prices when costs moved, you are full, or almost every quote is a yes. Set the date, say who keeps the old price, and watch close rate and margin after.
- [How to Decide Whether to Expand to a New Location or Market](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/should-you-expand/): Expand when the offer runs without you, someone else can run a normal day, and cash covers a slow start. Test small, and write the numbers that make you stop.
- [How to Allocate a Limited Budget](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/where-to-invest-next-dollar/): Put the next dollar on the constraint. Compare return, how fast cash comes back, and the cost of being wrong. Ignore sunk spend. Keep a buffer for payroll.
- [How to Run a Weekly Operating Review](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-run-a-weekly-operating-review/): Run a weekly operating review that turns missed targets into decisions. Choose a small scorecard, diagnose exceptions, and leave with owners and due dates.
- [How to Choose Business KPIs That Lead to Decisions](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-choose-business-kpis/): Choose business KPIs by starting with decisions, not dashboards. Define outcomes, leading signals, owners, and review rules that reveal the real constraint.
- [How to Fix Missed Deadlines Without Adding More Chasing](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-fix-missed-deadlines/): Fix missed deadlines by separating bad estimates, overloaded queues, and blocked decisions. Reset promises with evidence, then change how work gets released.
- [How to Plan Capacity Before Taking On More Work](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-plan-capacity-before-taking-on-more-work/): Check capacity before accepting more work. Estimate the constrained step, account for rework and existing promises, and compare hiring, pricing, and timing.
- [When to Hire Your First Operations Manager](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/when-to-hire-your-first-operations-manager/): Decide when to hire your first operations manager. Separate a management gap from broken processes, define decision rights, and test whether the role can pay.
- [How to Write a Hiring Scorecard](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-write-a-hiring-scorecard/): Write a hiring scorecard around outcomes, evidence, and decision rights. Compare candidates consistently and separate essential capability from preferences.
- [How to Decide Between Hiring and Outsourcing](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-decide-between-hiring-and-outsourcing/): Compare hiring and outsourcing using workload, control, ramp time, and total cost. Choose a reversible pilot before committing to a role or supplier contract.
- [How to Onboard a New Manager Without Keeping All the Decisions](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-onboard-a-new-manager/): Onboard a manager with clear outcomes, decision rights, and staged ownership. Set a baseline, transfer context, and review the handoff without undermining it.
- [What to Do When Cash Runway Drops Below Six Months](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/what-to-do-when-cash-runway-drops-below-six-months/): When cash runway falls below six months, build a weekly cash view, test downside assumptions, and rank actions by cash timing before making broad spending cuts.
- [How to Build a 13-Week Cash Flow Forecast](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-build-a-13-week-cash-flow-forecast/): Build a 13-week cash flow forecast from bank balances, receipts, and committed payments. Track uncertainty, explain variances, and turn shortfalls into action.
- [How to Handle a Customer Who Pays Late](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-handle-a-customer-who-pays-late/): Handle a late-paying customer by separating invoice errors, disputes, and cash problems. Set a clear collection plan and decide whether to extend more credit.
- [How to Decide Whether to Drop an Unprofitable Customer](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-decide-whether-to-drop-an-unprofitable-customer/): Decide whether to keep, reprice, or exit an unprofitable customer. Separate avoidable costs from overhead and compare cash timing, capacity, and alternatives.
- [How to Decide Which Product to Shut Down](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-decide-which-product-to-shut-down/): Decide which product to stop by comparing future contribution, strategic fit, and avoidable complexity. Test a focused repair and plan the customer transition.
- [How to Test a New Market Before Expanding](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-test-a-new-market-before-expanding/): Test a new market before committing fixed costs. Define the buyer and offer, seek paid demand, measure delivery economics, and set an explicit expansion gate.
- [How to Set Quarterly Business Priorities](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-set-quarterly-business-priorities/): Set quarterly priorities around the business constraint. Choose outcomes, price the capacity tradeoff, stop competing projects, and review evidence each week.
- [How to Decide Whether to Discount a Deal](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-decide-whether-to-discount-a-deal/): Decide whether to discount a deal by checking the real buying obstacle, contribution, capacity, and concessions. Trade price for something instead of hoping.
- [How to Handle an Underperforming Manager](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-handle-an-underperforming-manager/): Handle an underperforming manager with clear evidence, decision rights, and a bounded improvement plan. Separate a capability gap from a broken role or process.
- [How to Stop Every Decision Coming to the CEO](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-stop-every-decision-coming-to-the-ceo/): Stop decisions returning to the CEO. Map the approval queue, assign decision rights, define escalation rules, and review outcomes without taking work back.
- [How to Resolve Conflict Between Sales and Operations](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-resolve-conflict-between-sales-and-operations/): Resolve sales and operations conflict by tracing promises, capacity, and handoffs. Set an acceptance rule and make exceptions visible before a deal is sold.
- [How to Run Effective One-on-One Meetings](https://thinkoperator.com/guides/how-to-run-effective-one-on-one-meetings/): Run one-on-one meetings that unblock decisions and build judgment. Use the employee's agenda, specific feedback, commitments, and a reliable follow-up loop.

## Site information

- [Sitemap](https://thinkoperator.com/sitemap.xml): canonical public page URLs.
- [Privacy](https://thinkoperator.com/privacy/): local storage, optional leaderboard, and anonymous counts.

Illustrative scenarios and worked numbers are examples, not reports about real companies. For navigation, prefer the canonical page links above rather than URLs with start, referral, or other query parameters.
